entry.summary: DIIV's new A. G. Cook-produced record ZIRP! is officially out on Friday. Hear the new single "Dare Me" and watch its music video.
entry.content:
DIIV's new A. G. Cook-produced record ZIRP!, which just so happens to be our reigning Album Of The Week, is officially out on Friday. We've already heard early tracks "The Fountain," "Kid," and "Trillions," two of which made it onto our hallowed 5 Best Songs Of The Week lists. Today, we're getting one final single before the drop, "Dare Me," which continues fusing their shoegaze sensibilities with squiggly electronic textures. It also comes with an atmospheric music video, directed by Louie Kovatch, in which the band performs the song in an abandoned office while clad in the rumpled businesswear they've been sporting lately. Watch and listen below.

DIIV have several festival appearances in Europe coming up, and they've also announced a huge world tour kicking off in Australia in February and concluding in the UK in the end of June.

entry.title: Queens Of The Stone Age – “Run Away From The Mob”
entry.summary: Queens Of The Stone Age are releasing their new album 'Perfecth' on Friday, and today they're sharing closing track "Run Away From The Mob."
entry.content:
Queens Of The Stone Age are releasing their new album, the slightly infuriatingly titled Perfecth, on Friday. The last single from the record found newly minted silver fox Josh Homme wondering "Where The Goth Girls At?" Today, we're getting closing track "Run Away From The Mob," which originally dates back to the session for 2013's ...Like Clockwork and features Dave Grohl behind the drum kit.

"It's a letter, a last one, addressed to an oldest son," Homme explains. "'If you're reading this, everything went wrong, and here’s what you have to do.' The end is the sound of a father standing behind his son." An examination of mob mentality and the court of public opinion, the song builds from a mournful guitar figure to an explosive expression of unconditional loyalty. Listen below.

Perfecth is out 10/30 on Matador.

entry.title: Jim James Announces Memoir
entry.summary: Over the summer, Jim James released Wowed Out, his first solo album in eight years. Now, the My Morning Jacket frontman is announcing a memoir titled One Wonders. It hits the shelves next spring. The book, which is his first, follows his Louisville upbringing, his love for music, and his struggles with depression and drinking.…
entry.content:
Over the summer, Jim James released Wowed Out, his first solo album in eight years. Now, the My Morning Jacket frontman is announcing a memoir titled One Wonders. It hits the shelves next spring.

The book, which is his first, follows his Louisville upbringing, his love for music, and his struggles with depression and drinking. In a statement, he wrote, "If nothing else, I hope the main thing someone takes away from this book (aside from learning more about the joys and challenges of being a working artist and musician) is that it’s okay to ask for help. Everyone is going through some sort of challenge in this crazy world. IT IS POSSIBLE to find your way out of darkness and despair, and begin to enjoy the subtle, beautiful, everyday victories of simply being alive."

Read the full statement below.

Hello, friends! I am releasing a memoir!

Why? Why write this book? Why now?

As I’ve made good progress in therapy over the last five or six years, I’ve been doing a lot of reflecting on finding my voice — both as a singer, songwriter and musician, and as a person wandering the earth wondering…

what do I really want to SAY with my life overall?

As I reflect on my own musical journey (from first learning to play the guitar to creating music in the present day) and navigating the complexities of life in general, I have been thinking a lot about my elders. For so many of them, tradition was to never speak about yourself. You carried your victories and failures, your joys and horrors, quietly.

A thought kept making its way into my mind: wouldn’t things be lighter for all of us if we shared more with other people?

I feel like it’s our generation’s job to tear down those walls and share our triumphs and horrors.

When we do, we’ll find that we’re all walking around with the same things inside of us, the good and the bad.

It helps so much when we can find a way to let them out together, so that we can all begin to move toward a more peaceful and love-centered existence.

As if it WANTED this to happen and was WILLING it to happen, the Universe stepped in and began to line up the things I needed to write this book, bring it to life, and ACTUALLY PUBLISH it. And I began to realize its purpose:

Perhaps if I illustrated my journey, and how I began to deal with my own struggles with mental health, it could help people take a step toward getting out of their own darkness and depression.

If nothing else, I hope the main thing someone takes away from this book (aside from learning more about the joys and challenges of being a working artist and musician) is that it’s okay to ask for help. Everyone is going through some sort of challenge in this crazy world. IT IS POSSIBLE to find your way out of darkness and despair, and begin to enjoy the subtle, beautiful, everyday victories of simply being alive.

One Wonders will be available April 13, 2027 in hardcover and ebook, and as an audiobook, which I'll be reading. Additionally, Carmichael's Bookstore in Louisville will have autographed copies that you can preorder now.

One Wonders is out 4/13/27. Pre-order it here.

entry.title: Robyn Mashes Up Tinashe & Teddybears In The Live Lounge
entry.summary: Usually, people cover one song when they drop by the BBC Live Lounge. But Swedish cult-pop overlord Robyn can do more things than most people, so she covered two songs at the same time. Robyn is out promoting her 2026 album Sexistential right now, and she has released a ton of remixes since the album…
entry.content:
Usually, people cover one song when they drop by the BBC Live Lounge. But Swedish cult-pop overlord Robyn can do more things than most people, so she covered two songs at the same time. Robyn is out promoting her 2026 album Sexistential right now, and she has released a ton of remixes since the album dropped. In the Live Lounge, she had the brilliant idea to fuse Tinashe's "Popstar" with the Teddybears' "Punkrocker."

"Popstar" is the title track from Tinashe's new LP, which is among the very best albums of 2026. It's the reason we did a cover story on Tinashe. "Punkrocker" is the 2007 song that Iggy Pop made with Swedish dance-rock crew Teddybears, and it had a viral revival last year after it showed up in James Gunn's Superman movie. Robyn is another past Teddybears collaborator, and band member Klas Åhlund has been producing her tracks for decades. It makes perfect sense for Robyn to fuse those two statement-of-intent tracks, since she can call herself a popstar and a punkrocker at the same time if she wants.

In their Live Lounge performance, Robyn and her band start off with a frothy, vulnerable take on "Punkrocker" that swaps titular phrase for the term "popstar." Later on, they switch it up so that Robyn can warn you not to fall in love with a popstar. In Robyn's hands, the two songs form complementary shapes. Check out her performance below.

entry.content:
The rumors are true: Guided By Voices have announced their 45th album, Speculation And Gossip. It follows March's Crawlspace Of The Pantheon, and it arrives at the beginning of next year. The lead single "Designed For Use" is out today.

Robert Pollard told Rolling Stone that Speculation And Gossip was made during his obsession with Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon A Time In Hollywood and surrealism. "We went back to doing things remotely with each individual coming up with his own approach to sound, fidelity and instrumentation instead of playing all together," Pollard said. "I wanted more audible separation of the instruments and overall I was after more diversity in song structures, musical styles and lyrical content. I also wanted it to be much brighter, less heavy in overall tone than Crawlspace. On this one I just gave them genre references. Post punk, pop, prog, psych or combinations."

Hear "Designed For Use" below.

Earlier this year, we posted Manhunt, the collaborative record that Boldy made with New York rapper Rome Streetz. Since…
entry.content:
We can't keep up. We try, but we can't. The permanently weary Detroit underground rap fixture Boldy James makes so much music, and it's all worth hearing, but the neverending deluge can be hard to track. Earlier this year, we posted Manhunt, the collaborative record that Boldy made with New York rapper Rome Streetz. Since then, Boldy has released three new albums — Hook, Line & Sinker with Your Boy Posca, Trapper's Alley 3: Hell Or High Water with Nicholas Craven, and 1LB with Your Boy Posca again — and we didn't post any of them. Apologies to everyone, I guess especially Your Boy Posca. But we will not miss Boldy's newest record with Real Bad Man.

LA producer and label head Real Bad Man has teamed with Boldy James for past collaborative albums like 2020's Real Bad Boldy, 2022's Killing Nothing, and last year's Conversational Pieces. He has also made albums with people like Zelooperz and Kool Keith. Today, Boldy James and Real Bad Man once again join forces on the new album Strobelight. If you have heard any of their previous tracks, you know precisely the combination of clean, sample-heavy boom-bap and hard muttering that you will find here. I'm on my first listen right now, and it sounds good. Wiki, El Cousteau, Grip, and Taj make guest appearances. Listen below.

Barrie’s last album was 2022’s Barbara, and she hasn’t put out any singles of her own since 2023’s “Hard Candy,” though she did collaborate with Hot Chip’s Joe Goddard and contribute to a Margo Guryan tribute…
entry.content:
It's been a while since we've heard from Barrie Lindsay, the Brooklyn-based artist who records as just plain Barrie. Barrie's last album was 2022's Barbara, and she hasn't put out any singles of her own since 2023's "Hard Candy," though she did collaborate with Hot Chip's Joe Goddard and contribute to a Margo Guryan tribute album in 2024. Today, she's back.

Barrie's new single "Gloria" isn't a Them/Patti Smith cover or a Laura Branigan cover, though it has some of the same synthetic triumph as the latter song. Barrie's track starts out as a bright harpsichord workout before turning into buzzy, psychedelic synthpop. It's a very fun song, and Barrie says, "I’ve been working on this song for four years." Check it out below.

entry.title: This Is The Kit – “Safety Valve” (Feat. Richard Dawson)
entry.summary: Kate Stables has been making thoughtful indie folk-rock as This Is The Kit for so long, and we can always count on her to deliver. She did so last month with “Skip A Stone,” the lead single from new album Ghost Coat. The next single is a pensive duet with Richard Dawson titled “Safety Valve,”…
entry.content:
Kate Stables has been making thoughtful indie folk-rock as This Is The Kit for so long, and we can always count on her to deliver. She did so last month with "Skip A Stone," the lead single from new album Ghost Coat. The next single is a pensive duet with Richard Dawson titled "Safety Valve," and if you've paid attention to either of these artists over the years, the prospect of hearing them together is a must-click.

Stables offered this statement to FLOOD:

This is a song dedicated to friends who come to your rescue. A helping hand. Someone who listens and doesn’t judge. And getting out on your bike and feeling better.

Speaking of kind, non-judgemental people, I had been dreaming of asking Richard Dawson to sing on the new record and somehow managed to pluck up the courage to ask him to sing on this track. He graciously accepted the challenge and it immediately turned it into one of my favourite songs on the album. Absolute legend. Finest pipes in the business.

Listen below.

Ghost Coat is out 1/15 on Memphis Industries. Pre-order it here.

entry.title: Massive Attack’s Robert Del Naja Shares New Life Support Soundtrack
entry.summary: Massive Attack’s music has felt cinematic from its very beginnings, and it has appeared in god only knows how many movies and TV shows over the decades. Now, group member Robert “3D” Del Naja — who is not Banksy, it turns out — has shared the soundtrack for Life Support, a new documentary about a…
entry.content:
Massive Attack's music has felt cinematic from its very beginnings, and it has appeared in god only knows how many movies and TV shows over the decades. Now, group member Robert "3D" Del Naja — who is not Banksy, it turns out — has shared the soundtrack for Life Support, a new documentary about a team of medics attempting to operate under the nightmarish conditions in Gaza.

Robert Del Naja has been a vocal advocate for Palestinian people during the current genocide. Just last month, British police arrested him (for the second time) for holding a sign in support of Palestine Action, the protest group that the UK government has proscribed as a terrorist organization. So Del Naja's work on this documentary obviously aligns with his values.

Del Naja and Palestinian composer Habib Shehada Hanna contributed original music to the film, and Del Naja also worked with its producers to select songs for the soundtrack, which features artists like Kneecap, Yasmine Hamdan, and 47Soul. It's also got a track from the Five Techniques, the new project from Belfast producer David Holmes, that features Paul Weller and Róisín El Cherif. In a press release, Dej Naja says:

Given the magnitude and rawness of Life Support, it was humbling to be asked to compose work that could in some way enhance a second-hand experience of living the devastating realities for volunteer medics and Gazan civilians. We hope the range of compositions go some way to travelling the emotional quagmire — but also elevating the astounding human spirit and resilience displayed by the subjects of this film.

The soundtrack album is out now on [PIAS], with all proceeds going to benefit the Health Workers 4 Palestine solidarity fund. Check it out below.

entry.title: Kilby Block Party Announces 2027 Lineup
entry.summary: The Kilby Block Party festival: What a great weekend! I went to that fest for the first time this year, and I had a blast. Kilby is an indie-centric affair, but it’s a big-tent version of indie with room for all kinds of subgenres and definitions. It’s not too big and not too small, and…
entry.content:
The Kilby Block Party festival: What a great weekend! I went to that fest for the first time this year, and I had a blast. Kilby is an indie-centric affair, but it's a big-tent version of indie with room for all kinds of subgenres and definitions. It's not too big and not too small, and the festival grounds are pretty comfortable and easy to navigate even when it gets gross and rainy outside. It was the closest thing I've experienced to the late, lamented Pitchfork Music Festival, and I mean that as the highest praise. Today, Kilby Block Party's organizers unveil the lineup for next year's festival, and it looks really, really good.

Next year's Kilby headliners are Deftones, the Strokes, and Jungle. I don't quite understand how Jungle are festival headliners now, but maybe I'll just need to catch their show and find out for myself. But Deftones and the Strokes, despite sharing very little in common musically, are both past-generation stars who have really broken through to zoomer audiences; my daughter, for instance, loves both of them. The top of the bill also includes younger acts like Fontaines D.C., Slayyyter, and Lil Yachty, all strong picks. For my money, though, Kilby really comes into focus when you look at the fully stacked undercard.

Right now, Kilby has a few question-mark mysteries on its poster, so we don't quite have the full picture yet. (Are those reunions? Artists who just haven't announced tours yet? We'll find out!) There are a couple of classic-album playthrough sets — Two Door Cinema Club doing Tourist History and Whitney doing Light Upon The Lake. Deerhunter's Bradford Cox recently revived his solo project Atlas Sound, and that's on the bill. So is the Radio Dept., the Swedish weird-pop project that has gone fully inactive in recent years. Looks like they're back!

We've got a pretty healthy number of underground legends on that lineup, and you could probably spend the whole weekend, if you wanted, focusing on the classics, including Spoon, Hot Chip, Kim Gordon, Wolf Parade, and Mercury Rev. Do Joyce Manor count as legends by now? They sort of do, right? What about Silversun Pickups? Twin Peaks? I'm feeling myself get older as I type this paragraph, so let's move on.

On top of all that, we've got a huge selection of some of acts from the current indie festival landscape, including IDLES, Weyes Blood, Julien Baker, Kurt Vile, Wednesday, Ratboys, Westside Cowboy, Iceage, Erika de Casier, Phantogram, Grace Ives, Caroline Rose, Porches, Lip Critic, Quiet Light, Sextile, Lowertown, Greg Freeman, Victoryland, Current Joys, Wunderhorse, Racing Mount Pleasant, Frankie And The Witch Fingers, Madra Salach, Rocket, Prostitute, Bandalos Chinos, Annabelle Dinda, Tokyo Tea Room, Dillom, Rehash, Choir Boy, Truman Sinclair, Gapyear, Heathers, Bee Blackwell, Seeking The Sun, Olympic Deth, Bonneville, Auxo., Roo Nostalgia, Cool Banana, Rally, Stage Fright, and Lillies.

Next year's festival goes down May 14-16 at the Utah State Fairpark, a beautiful location. A KeyBank pre-sale for three-day passes starts right now, and apparently you don't need a KeyBank account to sign up. General on-sale for three-day passes begins 10/29 — that's tomorrow — at 10 a.m. mountain time. For more info, check over here.

entry.title: Tindersticks Announce New Album Dog Roses: Hear “Loving, Leaving”
entry.summary: For nearly 35 years now, Stuart Staples has led the culty, adventurous UK indie band Tindersticks, and he’s not slowing down now. In 2024, Tindersticks released the acclaimed and experimental album Soft Tissue. Last year, they headed out on their first North American tour in 16 years. And today, Tindersticks announce plans for their 15th…
entry.content:
For nearly 35 years now, Stuart Staples has led the culty, adventurous UK indie band Tindersticks, and he's not slowing down now. In 2024, Tindersticks released the acclaimed and experimental album Soft Tissue. Last year, they headed out on their first North American tour in 16 years. And today, Tindersticks announce plans for their 15th studio album.

The new Tindersticks LP is called Dog Roses, and it's set to arrive in March. It's the first that the band has made after leaving their longtime studio, recording instead at what a press release calls "a hidden underground studio." This time around, they're joined by electric guitarist Dave Okumu, of the Invisible, and saxophonist Julian Siegel. Here's what Stuart Staples says about the new LP in a press release:

With our last album, 2023’s Soft Tissue, we felt like we were looking over the fence into a new landscape, maybe even leaning over. Making 15 albums we have learned that sometimes there are steps forward, sometimes there are leaps. Soft Tissue was a great step, but it was time to try and leap over that fence...

Most things I have learned, that I thought I knew about making albums, proved to be of little use when making Dog Roses. I have always had a strong sense of time and place in my writing — but sometimes while making this album it felt like trying to catch only a fragrance or the feeling of the knot in my stomach, or catching a glance of myself in a mirror — the 1000 questions, thoughts, emotions you can feel in one moment.

Below, check out the album's lush lead single "Loving, Leaving" and the album's tracklist.

entry.title: nowhere else to be Announce Self-Titled Debut Album: Hear “r1 (ripples)”
entry.summary: nowhere else to be are an indie rock band from Montreal announcing their self-titled debut album and sharing its anthemic opening track.
entry.content:
nowhere else to be are an indie rock band from Montreal led by Oren Lefkowitz, who also releases music under the name Oscar Louis, and Chris Vincent. With a minimal online presence, deliberately fuzzy artwork, and press releases liberally redacted with black highlights, they seem to be intentionally cultivating an air of mystery. Fortunately, what they may lack in biographical detail, they more than make up for with their songs.

And there are a bunch of them already! The band has been quietly releasing a string of singles for the past six months: "hanna," margins of a scene," "across the line," "brother bear," and "higher! higher! (for Paul)." Today, they're officially announcing their debut self-titled album, out in December, and sharing its anthemic opening track "r1 (ripples)," which pairs some delicious guitar fuzz with a beautifully soaring vocal melody. According to the band:

"r1" is the album's thesis. A violent, beautiful birth. You are the result of everything that came before you, but you are also constantly influencing everything around you. That can destroy you or give you power.

The song moves through three emotional phases:

  1. the joy of feeling connected to something larger than yourself
  2. the tragedy of a man, Oren's father, strung out and alone, unable to carry that weight
  3. and then back to the opening question: aren't we all ripples?

Listen below, unless you have somewhere else to be.

entry.title: Kevin Morby – “Nursery Rhyme” (Feat. Lonnie Holley)
entry.summary: Earlier this year, Kevin Morby released the excellent album Little Wide Open and the one-off single “PBJ,” and he also became a dad. If I had to guess, I’d say that Morby’s new fatherhood has something to do with his decision to release the raw, angry protest song “Nursery Rhyme,” a six-minute bromide about living…
entry.content:
Earlier this year, Kevin Morby released the excellent album Little Wide Open and the one-off single "PBJ," and he also became a dad. If I had to guess, I'd say that Morby's new fatherhood has something to do with his decision to release the raw, angry protest song "Nursery Rhyme," a six-minute bromide about living in a society where your kids can just be killed at anytime because we're not willing to get rid of the guns that constantly surround us.

Morby says that he recorded "Nursery Rhyme" last year and that it's his "darkest and most violent song," which is why he has released it as a Bandcamp exclusive. It's a swirling march that ends with an appearance from the Alabama visual artist and musician Lonnie Holley. The way Morby puts it, the song stands as an angrier decade-later sequel to his 2016 protest song "Beautiful Strangers." The single release is a pay-what-you-want download, with all proceeds going to Everytown for Gun Safety. Here's what Morby says about it:

In light of recent events, I’ve decided to release a new song called "Nursery Rhyme" — a song I've had in my back pocket that I’ve been hesitant to release ever since recording it in summer of 2025.

It is far and away the darkest and most violent song I’ve ever written and because of that, I am releasing it on my Bandcamp only — a corner of the internet that one has to willingly go to, as I did not want to run the risk of the song popping up in any sort of algorithm or entering someone’s psyche without permission.

So, trigger warning: "Nursery Rhyme" contains themes of gun violence against children.

Themes, of course, that we are inundated with on our screens on a daily basis. Themes that, as a new father, make my heart break for the parents and their children in a way that was not possible before.

But writing "Nursery Rhyme" has provided a space for my anger to temporarily live. Maybe you can put some of your collective anger into listening to the song and maybe it can also provide you with a bit of catharsis. I hope so.

It’s hard to know what else to do in a country where the powers-that-be worship inside the church of weapons of mass destruction and value profits over the lives of our children. Sometimes you just gotta scream.

It is also not lost on me that, as we approach the tenth anniversary of "Beautiful Strangers," I have once again found myself writing another topical protest song surrounding gun violence in America. A decade on, though, this new song is much less optimistic than its predecessor.

With that being the case, I thought it important to bring in the mighty Lonnie Holley to come cleanse the air after my singing cuts out. Once the dust settles, Lonnie blesses the song with his wisdom and hope. Thank you, Lonnie. It’s such an honor to share some sonic space with you.

I recorded "Nursery Rhyme" after dropping into a session happening at Sam Cohen's studio last year while he was working with the great French band Petite-Vallée, and we ended up recording this song with them as the backing band. Cochemea Gastelum later stopped by to lay down some saxophone.

You can pay what you want for ‘Nursery Rhyme’ and all proceeds will go directly to Everytown For Gun Safety - an organization I wholeheartedly support and believe in.

entry.content:
Last year, the tremendously gifted Chicago rapper Saba finally released From The Private Collection Of Saba And No ID, his long-awaited full-length collaboration with the OG Chicago producer No ID. Now, Saba is back to making music with Pivot Gang, the tight-knit group of friends who he's been with since he first arrived on our radar.

Pivot Gang's new single "Location" is their first group effort since the 2024 single "Who At The Door." It's a lush, hazy, melodic posse cut. Crew member daedaePIVOT co-produced the track with Ben Nartey, and it's got Saba, MFnMelo, Joseph Chilliams, and Frsh Waters trading off playful lines without ever giving the impression that they're competing with each other — except in the ultra-casual JLEAN-directed video, where they all hang out in a basement and clearly want to prove their superiority at poker, pool, Uno, etc. Saba describes it as their version of a "That '70s Show-style cypher." Check it out below.

Pivot Gang just announced their annual John Walt Day concert, in honor of the crew member who was murdered in 2017. This year's edition goes down 12/19 at Thalia Hall; get tickets here.

entry.title: Everything But The Girl Announce New Album Blue Reservoir: Hear “Young And Dumb”
entry.summary: They got me with this one. Everything But The Girl, the long-running UK duo of married couple Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt, recently started releasing new music and playing live again after a decades-long break, and the first single from their upcoming album Blue Reservoir is all about aging and missing the version of yourself…
entry.content:
They got me with this one. Everything But The Girl, the long-running UK duo of married couple Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt, recently started releasing new music and playing live again after a decades-long break, and the first single from their upcoming album Blue Reservoir is all about aging and missing the version of yourself that did ridiculous, passionate, self-destructive things all the time. In a soft and husky rasp, Thorn sings, "Yes I’m older and wiser/ I know more than I did then/ But I’d give up all the wisdom to be young and dumb again." Whoof. That's too real. I'm not sure I was ready to confront that level of realness on a Wednesday morning in October.

Everything But The Girl started way back in 1982, and they went through a number of different styles, from the slinky sophisti-pop of their early days to the slinky drum 'n' bass that they adapted in the late '90s. (The sounds were different, but the slinkiness remained.) EBTG went inactive after 1999's Temperamental — great album — so that Thorn and Watt could focus on their solo careers. In 2023, they returned with the comeback album Fuse, which found them playing around with dance textures once again. Last year, they returned to performing live after a quarter century, playing a series of sold-out shows at the MOTH Club, a small London venue. Today, they announce Blue Reservoir, a new album directly inspired by their MOTH Club experience.

In a press release, Tracey Thorn talks about how much the duo enjoyed the experience of those MOTH Club shows: "There was an intensity and simplicity to the MOTH shows that took us back to how we started out. Direct, rooted in guitar and voice, a few extra colors. We hadn’t been in that world for a long time, and it just felt fresh and real."

In response, Ben Watt bought a Spanish nylon-string guitar, and the duo went back to writing the kind of lush, thoughtful songs that they made when they were starting out. Watt says, "It is the sound of so much of the music I first connected with growing up, and I’d never actually owned one. It became quite an emotional springboard for me. I found a voice I thought I’d lost."

"Young And Dumb," for instance, is a soft acoustic song with a lilting bossa nova rhythm. It's one of the songs that Everything But The Girl wrote earlier this year, drawing on Latin music and English folk. They recorded most of the album live at London's RAK Studios, with a band that included double bassist Rex Horan, drummer Evan Jenkins, and percussionist Fabio de Oliveira, those father Bosco was a big influence on Everything But The Girl's 1984 debut Eden. Thorn and Watt's son Blake Watt, now of the London indie-folk band Family Stereo, guests on two songs, and Ben Watt overdubbed in some extra stuff at home later.

Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt wrote the treatment for the "Young And Dumb" video, and Edward Bishop directed it, shooting it at the MOTH Club. It's a single-shot performance with a few surprises, and it really lets you focus on the song, which got under my skin immediately. Thorn and Watt are both in their sixties, and I find the song to be a beautiful way of reckoning with the passage of time. Check it out below.

TRACKLIST:
01 "Forward"
02 "Scala"
03 "Young And Dumb"
04 "Do What You Can"
05 "Christmas Gone"
06 "Courage Mon Brave"
07 "The Round And Round"
08 "Fork In The Road"
09 "Good Hope"
10 "The Great Unknown"

Blue Reservoir is out 2/19 on Buzzin' Fly/Virgin. Pre-order it here.

entry.title: My Chemical Romance Bow To Pressure From Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders
entry.summary: My Chemical Romance are out on the road performing their 2006 classic The Black Parade for its 20th anniversary. As is the band’s custom, the live show involves a great deal of pageantry, including a staged shootout involving fake Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders that took place at the Hollywood Bowl last Wednesday, then again on Thursday.…
entry.content:
My Chemical Romance are out on the road performing their 2006 classic The Black Parade for its 20th anniversary. As is the band's custom, the live show involves a great deal of pageantry, including a staged shootout involving fake Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders that took place at the Hollywood Bowl last Wednesday, then again on Thursday.

The real Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders got wind of this and filed a temporary restraining order and injunction against MCR, arguing that the performance might lead the public to believe the cheerleaders had signed off on this. Specifically, the cheerleaders' parent company Pro Silver Star Ltd. filed the lawsuit. In their complaint, Pro Silver Star alleged that the band ignored a cease-and-desist issued Thursday. They have not, however, ignored the legal action.

My Chemical Romance have agreed to stop using Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader lookalike uniforms in their live shows, TMZ reports. It's a somewhat surprising decision coming after legal experts told Billboard the DCC parody was likely protected under the First Amendment, but maybe Gerard Way did not want to go to court over this matter.

In other Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders news, they successfully unionized!

entry.title: Meiv – “No Future Pt. 1 & 2” (Feat. Armand Hammer)
entry.summary: Meiv have enlisted underground rap duo Armand Hammer and electronic producer Body Meat for their new single "No Future Pt. 1 & 2."
entry.content:
Meiv is the genre-hopping, geography-spanning project of Tokyo-based artist Curinus, his Hong Kong-based musical partner Eugene Nx, and the latter's young daughter Sara Nx. After introducing themselves last month with the kaleidoscopic debut single "Dedeoka," which was produced by American electronic artist Body Meat, they're back with another track.

For new single "No Future Pt. 1 & 2," Meiv have enlisted the talents of two more experimentalist weirdos: Armand Hammer, the consistently great duo of underground New York rappers ELUCID and billy woods. True to its name, the song unfolds in two distinct chapters, kicking off with nonsensically sing-song lyrics and colorful organ blurts before vibe-shifting into something decidedly more downbeat.
